# RG02 `privileged-step-in-exploit`: A step in the exploit runs as a privileged address

<!-- Generated by `realism-gate explain --markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Severity:** warn (warn; silenced by a realism.yaml `privileged:` entry)

The test body pranks as an address that reads as a role (owner, admin, keeper, ...) or impersonates a protocol contract.

## Why it matters

`vm.prank(admin)` in `setUp()` is configuration. The same line in the test body is a step of the exploit that the attacker cannot sign. Sometimes that is legitimate: a keeper harvests on a schedule, governance executes a passed proposal. Then the claim depends on that role acting, and the report has to say why the attacker can rely on it. Impersonating a protocol contract (`vm.prank(address(pool))`) is never something an attacker can do.

## How to fix it

Move configuration into `setUp()`. If the exploit genuinely depends on a routine privileged action, declare it in `realism.yaml` under `privileged:` with the role and the reason the attacker can count on it, and make the report say the same.

## Fires on

```solidity
function test_drain() public {
    vm.prank(admin);
    vault.setOracle(address(fakeOracle));
    vm.prank(attacker);
    vault.borrow(1_000e18);
}
```

## Does not fire on

```solidity
function test_drain() public {
    // The oracle is the live one; nothing privileged happens here.
    vm.prank(attacker);
    vault.borrow(1_000e18);
}
```

## Known false-positive modes

- A role word in an ordinary user's name (`managerOfFunds` for a user account). Rename the variable or declare it under `victim.identities`.
- `owner` used for an ERC-4626 share owner. Prefer `shareOwner` or `holder`, which the tool reads as a user.

## In Solana tests (Rust and Anchor TypeScript)

A transaction in the exploit is signed by a keypair that reads as a role (admin, authority, governance, keeper, ...) or that the harness gave a role.

**How to fix it:** Move configuration before the attacker's first transaction. If the exploit genuinely depends on a routine privileged action, declare it in `realism.yaml` under `privileged:` with the role and the reason the attacker can count on it, and make the report say the same.

### Fires on

```rust
send(&mut svm, &set_oracle_ix(&fake_oracle), &[&admin]);
send(&mut svm, &borrow_ix(&attacker.pubkey(), 1_000), &[&attacker]);
```

```typescript
await program.methods.setOracle(fakeOracle.publicKey).accounts({ admin: admin.publicKey }).signers([admin]).rpc();
await program.methods.borrow(new BN(1_000)).accounts({ borrower: attacker.publicKey }).signers([attacker]).rpc();
```

### Does not fire on

```rust
// The oracle is the live one; nothing privileged happens here.
send(&mut svm, &borrow_ix(&attacker.pubkey(), 1_000), &[&attacker]);
```

```typescript
// The oracle is the live one; nothing privileged happens here.
await program.methods.borrow(new BN(1_000)).accounts({ borrower: attacker.publicKey }).signers([attacker]).rpc();
```

### Known false-positive modes

- `authority` used for a user's own authority under a bare name. Prefer `user_authority` or the person's name, which the tool reads as a user.
- A keypair named for a role the program never checks. Rename it or add an `allow` comment.

## Silencing it

Add a comment on the line, or the line above, with a reason:

```solidity
// realism-gate: allow(RG02) <why this is not a defect here>
```

The comment is the same in Rust and TypeScript. A comment without a reason is ignored, and the output says so.
